weeks.title: Describing motion
weeks.description: Use a reference point to describe an object's position and how it changes over time. Distinguish an observation of motion from the choice of observer.

weeks.title: Distance and displacement
weeks.description: Compare total distance travelled with displacement from start to finish. Show displacement as a straight-line change in position with direction.

weeks.title: Scalars and vectors
weeks.description: Sort motion quantities into scalars and vectors. Represent displacement and velocity with direction, and explain why direction matters in motion problems.

weeks.title: Speed and velocity
weeks.description: Calculate average speed from distance and time, then compare it with average velocity. Show working and include suitable units and direction.

weeks.title: Speed equation practice
weeks.description: Rearrange speed = distance ? time to solve for each quantity. Solve multi-step word problems and check units and significant figures.

weeks.title: Converting speed units
weeks.description: Convert between metres per second and kilometres per hour. Estimate everyday speeds and use conversions to compare journeys fairly.

weeks.title: Measuring speed fairly
weeks.description: Measure the time taken to travel a known distance. Identify controlled variables, repeat trials, and calculate a reliable average speed.

weeks.title: Reliability and uncertainty
weeks.description: Compare repeated measurements, identify anomalous results, and describe timing and distance uncertainties. Suggest practical changes that improve data quality.

weeks.title: Position-time graphs
weeks.description: Plot position against time using labelled axes and an appropriate scale. Place data accurately and describe the motion represented by a graph.

weeks.title: Reading graph gradients
weeks.description: Relate the gradient of a position-time graph to velocity. Calculate gradients from straight sections and compare the motion of different objects.

weeks.title: Motion in stages
weeks.description: Interpret flat, straight, and changing sections on a position-time graph. Describe when an object is stationary, moving steadily, or changing velocity.

weeks.title: Relative motion
weeks.description: Compare the motion of two objects using reference frames and position-time data. Explain how an observer's motion can change the description of an event.

weeks.title: Velocity-time graphs
weeks.description: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph and connect the gradient to acceleration. Identify constant velocity, speeding up, and slowing down.

weeks.title: Calculating acceleration
weeks.description: Calculate acceleration from change in velocity divided by time. Rearrange the equation, convert units where needed, and interpret positive or negative results.

weeks.title: Gravity and free fall
weeks.description: Describe how gravity changes an object's velocity as it falls. Use g ? 9.8 m/s? for calculations and discuss the effect of air resistance.

weeks.title: Graphing a falling object
weeks.description: Use motion data or a simulation to plot a falling object's velocity over time. Estimate acceleration from the graph and compare it with gravitational acceleration.

weeks.title: Newton's first law and inertia
weeks.description: Use Newton's first law to explain why motion stays unchanged when forces are balanced. Relate inertia to mass with familiar examples.

weeks.title: Resultant force and F = ma
weeks.description: Find the resultant force in one dimension and use F = ma to calculate force, mass, or acceleration. State units and explain the direction of acceleration.

weeks.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces
weeks.description: Draw force diagrams and determine whether forces are balanced. Predict how the magnitude or direction of motion changes when a resultant force acts.

weeks.title: Newton's third law
weeks.description: Identify equal and opposite interaction forces acting on different objects. Use examples such as walking, swimming, and vehicle motion to explain the law.

weeks.title: Friction and air resistance
weeks.description: Investigate how friction and drag affect moving objects. Identify factors that change resistive forces and relate them to acceleration.

weeks.title: Terminal velocity
weeks.description: Explain how a falling object's weight and air resistance change during a fall. Use a force diagram to show why acceleration reaches zero at terminal velocity.

weeks.title: Momentum and collisions
weeks.description: Calculate momentum using p = mv and apply conservation of momentum to simple one-dimensional interactions. Track direction with signs.

weeks.title: Motion design challenge
weeks.description: Analyse a motion scenario using graphs, force ideas, or momentum. Present a claim supported by calculations or data, and evaluate the evidence.
